newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close firm, off day's highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close firm, off day's highs.

text.p: French shares finished higher but off their session highs due to a softer dollar tone and weakness in morning trading on Wall Street, traders said.

Profit-taking on the last day of the April account also meant the CAC index failed to break through resistance at 2,550. The CAC had rebounded sharply at the opening, helped by the Dow's sharp rise on Tuesday and a generally strong dollar.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 18.97 points or 0.75 percent at 2,533.64. The CAC-40 futures contract was up 21 at 2,536 from Tuesday's close.
* Political risk seen waning for the time being, helped by a CSA opinion poll which showed the centre-right coalition being returned with a comfortable majority, even though reduced.

* AGF falls 3.63 percent to 183.6 francs, with one analyst concerned about the dilutive effect of its four billion franc convertible bond issue and said it ran counter to the chairman's promise at privatisation that there would be no dilutive moves.
However, other brokers were less worried about the dilution but the market talk was that the funds would be used to buy GAN . Gan closed up 7.45 percent at 150.

* Accor reported after the close 1996 net attributable profit of 1.06 billion francs and an unchanged net dividend of 20 francs per share. The stock closed up 4.13 percent at 883 on anticipation of the figures.
* Rhone-Poulenc added 2.24 percent to 182.5 francs, helped by a forecast 1997 assets sales would raise five billion francs rather than three billion.
* Cie Bancaire firms 2.67 pecent to 769, supported by recurrent speculation over a sale of Cetelem, which was up 1.38 percent at 663.
* Pricing of fresh sale of Bull shares welcomed.

* One fund manager said, "It's a bargain, or rather the price corresponds with the risk confronting the group". Another said "The price is alright. It's a gamble but if you win, there's a lot of money to be made.
The government is selling 16.2 million Bull shares, at 38 francs per share to institutions and 36 francs to retail investors.
* Filipacchi gained 9.88 percent to 1,379 francs, helped by a positive analysts meeting in which the company said first quarter advertising revenues showed a strong rise.
